entities.summary: Guillem Soler, a Majorcan cartographer, produced a significant work during the 14th century. His cartographic output reflected the cultural exchange between the Mediterranean and the Islamic world. This exchange had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic geography. Soler's work also demonstrates the growing influence of European cartography during this period. His cartographic legacy has been studied by historians of cartography, who note the importance of his contributions to the field. Soler's work reflects the cultural exchange between the Mediterranean and the Islamic world, as well as the growing influence of European cartography during the 14th century. The cartographic output of the Islamic world during this period also had a lasting impact on the development of European geography and cartography. Soler's work is an example of the complex cultural exchange that occurred between the Mediterranean and the Islamic world during this period. His cartographic output has been studied by historians of cartography, who note the importance of his contributions to the field. The legacy of Soler's work can be seen in the development of modern cartography and geography.
